To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a combined methodology for ICM isolation and derivation of ES cell lines using whole-blastocysts and laser drilling technology.

the combination of whole blastocyst culture followed laser drilling technology significantly enhances the efficiency of ICM isolation and embryonic cell derivation from both good- and poorquality mouse blastocysts.

the efficiency of inner-cell mass (ICM)-isolation and embryonic stem (ES) cell derivation from mouse embryos is significantly superior to that of either whole-blastocysts culture or laser-drilling technology alone.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a novel method for improving the efficiency in the derivation of ES cell lines using mouse embryos.
the optimization of the derivation of mouse ES cell lines, which may provide a new strategy to improve the derivation of hESC lines from human embryos that are otherwise not suitable for derivation.
improving the efficiency of ES cell derivation and may be of interest to the hES cell field, as it provides a strategy for improving the derivation of hESC lines using a new combined methodology.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the combination of whole-embryo culture and laser drilling technology significantly improves ICM isolation and subsequent ES cell derivation from mouse embryos, regardless of quality.
the combination of laser drilling and whole-blastocysts culture is a promising method for improving the efficiency and success rate of ES cell derivation, especially from poor-quality embryos.
the combined methodology is the most effective way to derive ES cells using either good- or poor-quality embryos.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the whole-blastocysts culture followed by laser destruction of the trophotoderm is a new, simple, and effective approach for the isolation of ICM from both good- and poorquality embryos, which is superior to the traditional methods of ICM isolation.
the whole-blastocysts are cultured to the blastocyst stage and then laser drilled, which allows the ICM to be isolated and then cultured on feeder layers.

the combination of whole-embryo culture followed by laser-assisted drilling technology is superior to whole-blas-tocyst culture or to laser drilling technology itself for improving the efficiency for ICM isolation and for the establishment of ES cell lines from both good-quality and poor-quality embryos.
The main takeaway from our work is that

this new strategy can be successfully applied not only to poor-quality mouse embryos but also to frozen poor-quality human embryos that would otherwise not be suitable for ICM isolation and derivation of ES cell lines using laser drilling technology or immunosurgery.
the combination of laser drilling and whole-blastocysts can significantly increase the efficiency of ICM isolation and derivation of ES cells from both poor- and good-quality mouse embryos.

the combined use of the whole-blastocysts culture and laser drilling technology can significantly increase the efficiency of both the ICM isolation and derivation of murine ES cells, regardless of the quality of the blastocyst.
